 --> Gold prices fall 26% from peak: Should buyers expect further correction or a rebound?
 Over two to three months, metal is building a base in strong accumulation zones and could rebound 10–15 percent, says report. 
 Dipen Pradhan 
 October 23, 2026 / 12:00 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Gold prices fall 26 percent from their record peak.
 Geopolitical tensions and inflation weigh on bullion.
 Analysts expect gold to remain volatile in the near term.

 Gold prices face a crucial test as they remain 26 percent below their all-time peak amid renewed tensions in the Middle East over the US-Iran conflict. Stubborn inflation, largely fuelled by high energy costs from the war, has also weighed on tighter monetary policy, putting pressure on bullion.
 Commodity analysts, however, say the current correction does not end gold’s broader rally, as geopolitical uncertainty and central-bank buying continue to support prices.
 "A stronger US dollar and rising Treasury yields are additional headwinds for the precious metal, while liquidation of positions after the recent rally has added to the decline," Nirpendra Yadav, Sr. Research Analyst at Bonanza Portfolio, said.
 He added, "However, the current correction does not necessarily signal the end of the broader bullish trend, as geopolitical uncertainty and central-bank buying could continue to provide underlying support."

 Spot gold prices surged to a record $5,419 per ounce on January 28, 2026. Fast forward to October 23, and the metal has fallen more than 26 percent to just above $4,007 per ounce.
 A similar trend was seen in the domestic market, with MCX spot gold surging to a record Rs 1,76,306 per 10 grams on January 29. Prices fell sharply to Rs 1,47,878 just three days later. This year, gold fell to a low of Rs 1,39,843 on June 25 and hovered near Rs 1,42,800 on October 22.
 In the futures market, gold was trading at Rs 1,42,249 per 10 grams on October 23 (09:28 IST) for December 4 delivery. This year, the metal's price on MCX surged to a peak of Rs 2,47,917 per 10 grams in January.
 Spot gold tracks the current market price for immediate purchase and delivery of physical gold, while gold futures are standardised exchange contracts to buy or sell gold at a predetermined price for delivery on a specified future date.
 According to Rupsha Chainani, Chief Research Officer at Augmont, gold is heading for its steepest drop in four months as high oil prices strengthen expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates.
 A stronger dollar and elevated crude oil prices continue to weigh on gold. The dollar index was trading 0.04 percent higher at 101.64 in the morning session, while Brent crude marked a 5-month high recently and is still up 0.42 percent in the last 24 hours to $113.65 per barrel in futures trade, keeping the bullion on edge.
 Gold outlook for investors 
 Going forward, investors should closely watch the Fed’s October 27–28 meeting, next week’s PCE inflation data, gold ETF flows, and developments in geopolitical tensions. In India, rupee movements can also influence domestic prices.
 Yadav suggests, "Investors should avoid aggressive buying during periods of volatility and consider staggered purchases based on their investment horizon and risk appetite."
 Analysts estimate gold is likely to remain volatile and may slide to $3,950 (Rs 1,40,000) in the near term. "Over two to three months, metal is building a base in strong accumulation zones and could rebound 10–15 percent. A sustained move above $4,200 for gold would confirm the start of a fresh uptrend," Chainani said.
